newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank's Citizens buys U.S. bank Grove.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank's Citizens buys U.S. bank Grove.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland Plc said on Monday its U.S. unit Citizens Financial Group had agreed to buy Grove Bank of Massachusetts for $87 million, payable in cash.

"This price represents around 1.8 times the estimated book value of Grove at completion and includes Greater Boston Bank, whose acquisition by Grove was announced in August 1996," the bank said in a statement.
At September 30, Grove had total assets of $599 million and seven branches in metropolitan Boston, whilst Greater Boston had assets of $167 million and three branches in Boston.
Royal Bank added it expected Citizens to fund the acquisition from its own resources.
Royal Bank of Scotland owns 76.5 percent of Citizens, with the remainder held by Bank of Ireland.
After this acquisition, Citizens, based in Providence, Rhode Island, will have 240 branches in four New England states and assets of around $16 billion.
Citizens' network in Boston will grow to 78 branches.
"This acquisition is consistent with our strategic objective of expanding...selectively in Massachusetts and Connecticut," Royal Bank chief executive George Mathewson said.
The buy was the tenth acquisition by Citizens since 1992.
